title: Special Report: Republican? Democrat? We Don't Take a Side. Here Are the Election Results That Affect La Cañada Flintridge.
author: lacanada.us editorial staff
image_alt: Voter at a voting booth inside a public library
excerpt: Preliminary November 3, 2026 election results for races and measures affecting La Cañada Flintridge, including the LCUSD board, local water districts, county measures, and statewide propositions. Results are not yet certified.
body_markdown:
The November 3, 2026, general election included decisions affecting La Cañada Flintridge residents, from seats on the La Cañada Unified School District Board of Education to representation in Sacramento and Washington, judicial elections, and statewide ballot propositions.

Rather than covering every political contest in California, this report focuses on races and ballot measures relevant to La Cañada Flintridge, including the reported results and the responsibilities or provisions involved.

> **IMPORTANT: RESULTS ARE PRELIMINARY AND NOT YET CERTIFIED.** This article is a snapshot published November 12, 2026, not a final election record. Local race totals are from the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk's **November 10, 2026** update, unless otherwise indicated. Statewide proposition outcomes reflect reporting available on **November 12, 2026**; media projections are not official certification. Ballots are still being processed, vote totals and percentages may change, and a leading candidate or measure is not necessarily the certified winner. **Readers should independently verify the latest official results and applicable ballot-measure language before making any financial, legal, civic, or other decisions based on election outcomes.** The official sources are linked throughout this article and listed at the end. Los Angeles County has scheduled its next update for November 13, 2026. The county plans to certify on November 27; California's statewide certification is scheduled for December 11. [Sources: Los Angeles County election updates](https://www.lavote.gov/home/voting-elections/current-elections/election-results), [county election media kit](https://content.lavote.gov/docs/rrcc/documents/media-kit_final.pdf), [California Secretary of State election calendar](https://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/upcoming-elections/general-election-november-3-2026/key-dates-deadlines).

## La Cañada Unified School District Board of Education

Three seats on the La Cañada Unified School District Governing Board were contested. Five candidates competed for positions overseeing district policy, budgets, educational priorities, and the superintendent.

*Districtwide, preliminary results reported November 10, 2026. Voters could select up to three candidates, so the percentages are shares of all candidate votes, not shares of voters.*

| Candidate | Votes | Share of candidate votes |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Dan Jeffries** | **5,814** | **26.8%** |
| **Susan Moore** | **5,008** | **23.1%** |
| **Octavia Thuss** | **4,640** | **21.4%** |
| Amarpreet Singh Malik | 3,387 | 15.6% |
| Shilpa Shinde-Garg | 2,830 | 13.1% |

Jeffries, Moore, and Thuss hold the three leading positions in the preliminary count. These are school-district totals, not solely votes cast within La Cañada Flintridge city limits.

*Source: [Los Angeles County official election returns — Schools](https://results.lavote.gov/text-results/4348).*

## Pasadena City College: Board of Trustees and Bond Measure

La Cañada Flintridge is part of the Pasadena Area Community College District, which operates Pasadena City College.

### Board of Trustees — Area 1

| Candidate | Votes | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Geoff Baum** | **12,597** | **56.3%** |
| Francis Pollara | 9,764 | 43.7% |

Baum leads the election for Trustee Area 1. The Board of Trustees governs Pasadena City College, including educational programs, district finances, facilities, and administrative policies.

### Measure UP — Pasadena City College Facilities

**Passing in the preliminary count; the measure requires 55% approval.**

| Vote | Votes | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Yes** | **103,734** | **74.8%** |
| No | 34,900 | 25.2% |

Measure UP authorizes up to $485 million in bonds for college classrooms, career-training facilities, repairs, and infrastructure. According to the ballot language, the district's bond tax rate would not exceed the existing $9 per $100,000 of assessed property value, with an estimated $27 million raised annually while the bonds are outstanding. The measure also specifies independent oversight and local control of expenditures.

*Source: [Los Angeles County official election returns — Pasadena Area Community College District](https://results.lavote.gov/text-results/4348).*

## Local Water District Elections

Three water agencies serving parts of La Cañada Flintridge or its immediate area had contested board elections. The totals below are **districtwide**, not city-only. Each district's boundaries determine which residents vote in its contests.

### Foothill Municipal Water District — Division 4

| Candidate | Votes | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Amy I. Chen** | **5,368** | **74.9%** |
| Laura Olhasso | 1,799 | 25.1% |

Chen leads the race. Foothill Municipal Water District supplies wholesale water to local retail water agencies; its board oversees water supply planning and related infrastructure and financial decisions.

### La Cañada Irrigation District — Division 4

| Candidate | Votes | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Helen Grace Avila Olivares** | **539** | **69.4%** |
| Sheree Rae Butts | 238 | 30.6% |

Olivares leads the race. La Cañada Irrigation District provides retail water service within its service area.

### Crescenta Valley Water District — Board of Directors

*Three seats; voters could select up to three candidates. Percentages are shares of candidate votes.*

| Candidate | Votes | Share of candidate votes |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Carla D. Dillon** | **4,506** | **33.3%** |
| **James Bodnar** | **4,252** | **31.4%** |
| **Jeffery W. Johnson** | **3,656** | **27.0%** |
| Alec Hyeler | 1,122 | 8.3% |

Dillon, Bodnar, and Johnson lead for the three available seats. The Crescenta Valley Water District election appeared on ballots in a portion of La Cañada Flintridge, as reflected in the county's city-level report.

*Sources: [Los Angeles County official election returns — Water Districts](https://results.lavote.gov/text-results/4348); [Votes Cast by Community, La Cañada Flintridge, pages 77–78 (November 4)](https://content.lavote.gov/docs/rrcc/svc/4348_community.pdf).*

## Representation in Sacramento and Washington

### California State Assembly — District 41

*Los Angeles County portion of the district only; the district also extends into San Bernardino County.*

| Candidate | LA County votes | LA County share |
|---|---:|---:|
| **John Harabedian (D)** | **106,006** | **72.5%** |
| Adam Christopher Vena (R) | 40,205 | 27.5% |

Harabedian leads in the Los Angeles County count. Assembly members vote on state legislation, taxation, budgets, education, transportation, public safety, housing, and other state matters. **These figures are not the complete districtwide totals and should not be used alone to determine the certified district result.**

### U.S. House of Representatives — District 28

*Los Angeles County portion of the district only; the district also extends into San Bernardino County.*

| Candidate | LA County votes | LA County share |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Judy Chu (D)** | **153,994** | **74.5%** |
| April A. Verlato (R) | 52,621 | 25.5% |

Chu leads in the Los Angeles County count. **These figures are not the complete districtwide totals and should not be used alone to determine the certified district result.**

California's 28th Congressional District includes La Cañada Flintridge and neighboring communities in the San Gabriel Valley. Its representative serves as the community's elected voice in the U.S. House of Representatives.

*Sources: [Los Angeles County official election returns — U.S. House and Assembly](https://results.lavote.gov/text-results/4348); [California Secretary of State statewide results](https://electionresults.sos.ca.gov/) (for complete multi-county totals).*

## Los Angeles County Sheriff

| Candidate | Votes | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Robert G. Luna** | **1,985,738** | **70.2%** |
| Alex Villanueva | 841,506 | 29.8% |

Incumbent Sheriff Robert Luna leads the countywide contest. The Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department provides law enforcement in La Cañada Flintridge through the Crescenta Valley Sheriff's Station. The department also administers county jails and provides court security.

*Sources: [Los Angeles County official election returns — Sheriff](https://results.lavote.gov/text-results/4348); [City of La Cañada Flintridge — Public Safety](https://lcf.ca.gov/public-safety/).*

## Los Angeles County Ballot Measures

These countywide measures also appeared on ballots in La Cañada Flintridge.

### Measure A — Public Safety Labor Arbitration

**Passing in the preliminary count.**

| Vote | Votes | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Yes** | **1,678,706** | **62.2%** |
| No | 1,020,797 | 37.8% |

Measure A amends the county charter to prohibit strikes by specified county public safety and related employees, reiterate requirements for good-faith negotiations, and establish impartial binding arbitration for certain disputes involving certified public safety employee organizations.

### Measure E — County Ethics Commission

**Passing in the preliminary count.**

| Vote | Votes | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| **Yes** | **2,006,529** | **75.1%** |
| No | 664,523 | 24.9% |

Measure E amends the county charter to provide more independence and structure for the Los Angeles County Ethics Commission, Office of Ethics Compliance, and Ethics Compliance Officer, including appointment processes, qualifications, terms, duties, and responsibilities. The measure also addresses the county's existing commitment to community investment and alternatives to incarceration.

*Source: [Los Angeles County official election returns — County Measures A and E](https://results.lavote.gov/text-results/4348).*

## California Statewide Ballot Propositions

California voters considered 14 statewide propositions on November 3. The descriptions below are based on the California Secretary of State's **Official Voter Information Guide**. The reported status column distinguishes Associated Press projections from contests still showing a lead without an AP call; **none of these are certified outcomes**. Statewide standings were reviewed November 12, 2026.

| Proposition | What it would do | Reported status (Nov. 12) |
|---|---|---|
| **[1 — Housing bonds](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/1/)** | Authorizes $11.25 billion in state general obligation bonds for affordable housing programs, including housing for veterans and other qualifying residents. | **Yes — AP projects passage** |
| **[2 — State reserves](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/2/)** | Expands California's rainy-day reserve requirements. | **Yes — AP projects passage** |
| **[3 — High-income taxes](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/3/)** | Makes existing higher state income-tax rates on high earners permanent instead of expiring in 2031, preserving funding for schools and health care. | **Yes — AP projects passage** |
| **[4 — Campaign financing](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/4/)** | Repeals California's prohibition on public financing of election campaigns, allowing governments to adopt such programs. | **No leads — uncalled** |
| **[5 — Statewide recall elections](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/5/)** | Changes replacement procedures following recalls of statewide officers; vacancy filling would occur by later election or appointment rather than a replacement vote on the recall ballot. | **Yes — AP projects passage** |
| **[37 — New-homebuyer loans](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/37/)** | Authorizes up to $25 billion in revenue bonds for loans to eligible middle-income buyers of qualifying newly constructed homes. | **Yes — AP projects passage** |
| **[38 — Medical research bonds](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/38/)** | Authorizes $8.4 billion in state general obligation bonds to finance immunology and immunotherapy research. | **Yes — AP projects passage** |
| **[39 — Voter identification](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/39/)** | Adds government-issued identification requirements for in-person voting and identifying-number requirements for mailed ballots. | **No — AP projects failure** |
| **[40 — One-time wealth tax](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/40/)** | Imposes a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of certain taxpayers with more than $1 billion in assets, primarily to fund health care. | **No — AP projects failure** |
| **[41 — State tax restrictions and audits](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/41/)** | Restricts new state taxes that exempt revenue from the state spending limit and requires audits related to new special taxes. | **No — AP projects failure** |
| **[42 — Personal-property and retroactive taxes](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/42/)** | Prohibits new state taxes on ownership of personal property, including financial assets, and certain retroactive state taxes. | **Yes leads — uncalled** |
| **[43 — Voter-proposed local special taxes](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/43/)** | Raises the approval threshold for voter-proposed local special taxes from a simple majority to two-thirds, beginning in 2027. | **No — AP projects failure** |
| **[44 — Health clinics](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/44/)** | Requires certain nonprofit community health clinics to devote at least 90% of revenue to qualifying program services, including but not limited to direct patient services. | **No — AP projects failure** |
| **[45 — Environmental review](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/45/)** | Changes California Environmental Quality Act review and legal challenge procedures for certain projects, including deadlines and scope of review. | **No — AP projects failure** |

Proposition numbers are not consecutive because they were assigned through different qualification procedures. The statewide measures apply according to their individual provisions and eligibility requirements, not through separate rules specific to La Cañada Flintridge.

*Sources: [California Secretary of State — Official Voter Information Guide](https://voterguide.sos.ca.gov/propositions/) (each proposition's individual official description is linked above); [KQED/AP — November 2026 statewide election standings and race calls](https://www.kqed.org/elections/results/california/); [California Secretary of State — live election results](https://electionresults.sos.ca.gov/).*

## Judicial Elections Affecting La Cañada Flintridge

Los Angeles County Superior Court judges hear civil, criminal, family, probate, and other matters throughout the county, including cases involving La Cañada Flintridge residents. Four contested Superior Court offices appeared on the November ballot.

*Countywide preliminary results, November 10, 2026.*

| Superior Court office | Leading candidate | Votes | Share |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Office 64 | **Maria Ghobadi** | **1,323,853** | **51.7%** |
| Office 65 | **Justin Allen Clayton** | **1,387,051** | **56.7%** |
| Office 87 | **Anthony (A.J.) Bayne** | **1,357,173** | **55.4%** |
| Office 131 | **Donna Tryfman** | **1,204,691** | **50.1%** |

Ghobadi leads Rhonda A. Haymon; Clayton leads Anna Slotky Reitano; Bayne leads David DeJute; and Tryfman leads David Ross. Office 131 remains a close contest: Tryfman's reported lead was **5,604 votes** in the November 10 count.

Voters also decided whether to retain California Supreme Court Justices **Joshua Groban** and **Kelli M. Evans**, as well as justices of the **Second District Court of Appeal**, which reviews cases from Los Angeles County Superior Court. The Los Angeles County count shows Yes majorities for both named Supreme Court justices and the Second District appellate justices listed on local ballots. In these retention elections, voters select Yes or No rather than choose between competing candidates.

Judges and justices serving on these courts may issue rulings in cases affecting La Cañada Flintridge residents, businesses, or local government. They do not represent the city as elected legislators do.

*Sources: [Los Angeles County official election returns — Superior Court and judicial retention](https://results.lavote.gov/text-results/4348); [California Courts — Second Appellate District](https://appellate.courts.ca.gov/district-courts/2dca/about); [California Courts — Judicial selection](https://newsroom.courts.ca.gov/branch-facts/judicial-selection-how-california-chooses-its-judges-and-justices).*

## When Will the Results Be Final?

Los Angeles County continues its post-election canvass, including eligible outstanding vote-by-mail ballots, provisional ballots, and ballots cast through conditional voter registration. The next county update is scheduled for **November 13, 2026**. Los Angeles County's published schedule targets **November 27** for county certification; state law sets **December 3** as the deadline for county certification, with the California Secretary of State scheduled to certify statewide results on **December 11, 2026**.

Before relying on any race or proposition result, readers should review the latest official returns. Numbers and status statements in this November 12 article may become outdated as additional ballots are counted and certification proceeds.
